The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola.
It is unclear when she arrived in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country.

articles.title_original: Zelensky says US intelligence sharing 'works now' after talks with Trump envoy in Oslo
articles.title_zh: Zelensky says US intelligence sharing 'works now' after talks with Trump envoy in Oslo
facts_zh:
Zelensky says US intelligence sharing 'works now' after talks with Trump envoy in Oslo
- Published
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has said US intelligence sharing on deadly Russian missile attacks "works now" after talks with President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff.
The meeting in Oslo came after accusations by Kyiv that Washington was withholding key intelligence - a claim rejected as "scandalous" by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
Finnish President Alexander Stubb, who also took part in the talks, said "genuine progress" was made on proposals to achieve peace but gave no details and warned that patience would be needed.

The researchers have been at the heart of an ongoing dispute over research on African newborns, supported by $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and matched by the Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation for a total of $3.2m.
